newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 12.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 12.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Wednesday:
* On Tuesday, the Dow Jones rose 51.57 points to 6,858.11. PLDT's ADR increased by $1 to $60.
* The peso closed up at 26.345 to a U.S. dollar from 26.349.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange composite index dropped 27.32 points to 3,358.70.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average steady at 10.5625 percent.
*Crown Equities Corp said on Tuesday its net income soared to 62 million pesos in 1996 from the previous two million pesos.
*Three Philippine companies said on Tuesday they have signed an agreement to participate in the construction of a $300 million cement plant in Cebu island.
Aboitiz Equity Ventures Inc, House of Investment Inc and Pacific Cement Co Inc told the Philippine Stock Exchange that they have signed an agreement to form South Western Cement Corp.

On Monday, British building materials group Blue Circle Industries Plc said in London it would hold 20 percent in the joint venture and operate the project and plant. Japan's Nissho Iwai Corporation and Philippine firm Lo-oc Limestone and Development Corp will also take equity in the project, Aboitiz said.

*Uniwide Holdings Inc said its board approved the issuance of 2.5 billion pesos worth of long-term commercial papers.The firm told the Philppine Stock Exchange, it said its board also decided to raise the franchise fee for all Uniwide Warehouse Clubs to two from one percent of net sales.
* Pilipino Telephone Corp said on Tuesday that Ignatius Yenko, its chief financial officer, had resigned effective February 15.

It said in a statement to the Philippine Stock Exchange that the resignation had been accepted. The Manila Times newspaper said Yenko had submitted his resignation because of a 740-million-peso writeoff in the 1996 year due to subscriber fraud and cloning.

Piltel said earlier this month that it expects net income in 1996 to reach around 700 million pesos despite the provision of 887 million pesos for doubtful accounts. The doubtful accounts include the 740 million pesos written off as bad debts.
*Universal Rightfield Property Holdings Inc is expected to post a net income of one billion pesos in 1997, parent firm DMCI Holdings said on Tuesday.
* Construction firm DMCI Holdings Inc plans to build a $250 million cement plant in Semirara island in the central Philippines, President Isidro Consunji told analysts at a briefing on Tuesday.
Consunji also said his company is set to sign a six-billion peso construction contract with Rockwell Land Corp, a unit of Benpres Holdings Corp, by the end of this month.
*Southeast Asia Cement Holdings Inc said on Tuesday its unaudited net income in 1996 reached 1.053 billion pesos, equivalent to an earnings per share of 0.207 pesos.
*Ionics Circuits Inc said its 1996 net reached 391.07 million pesos against the previous 284.17 million.
*Philex Mining Corp, the country's largest gold mining company, expects to make a net profit of 507 million pesos this year, company chairman Gerard Brimo said on Tuesday.

Increased output of 341,000 ounces of gold from three mine fields will help earnings, Brimo told Reuters in a telephone interview. Last year, the company produced 181,083 ounces last year from two mines.
Brimo said the company projected the price of gold to rise to $365 per ounce from the current $340.
Philex posted a net income of 1.4 billion pesos in 1996 including extraordinaries compared with 369 million pesos in 1995, Brimo said.
